Action Plan:
1. Urgent neurology referral for evaluation of progressive left arm numbness/tingling and weakness and a transient left-eye visual disturbance; clinician discussed concern for a possible demyelinating process (e.g., multiple sclerosis). Referral may include brain imaging per neurology.
2. Safety-net advice: Attend Emergency Department if symptoms worsen or new red flags occur, including progression of weakness to legs, severe or worsening headache, vomiting, seizures/fits, or worsening/persistent visual symptoms.
3. No new medications initiated pending specialist assessment; steroids were discussed as potential treatment only after a confirmed diagnosis.
4. Verbal consent from patient has been obtained before using transcription software.

Subjective:
- Reason for visit: Progressive left arm numbness/tingling and perceived weakness; intermittent shoulder discomfort with movement.
- History of present illness:
  - Onset ~2 weeks ago after starting a boxing class a few weeks prior.
  - Symptoms have progressed from mild tingling to persistent numbness and tingling.
  - Distribution: Left upper limb; tingling/numbness most notable in digits 2–4 on the palmar (front) side; involves elbow, arm, and hand; difficulty with piano accuracy; can grasp a glass (primarily right-hand dominant).
  - Pain: Not primary driver of weakness; occasional left shoulder pain with boxing movements; at rest feels numb/tingly.
  - Self-care tried: Massage and warm baths—no improvement.
- Associated symptoms:
  - Transient visual disturbance: Loss of part of the visual field in the left eye lasting ~20 minutes a few weeks ago; resolved spontaneously.
  - Headaches: Occasional “tired” headaches; fatigue reported.
  - Seizures: Denied.
  - Neck pain: Patient initially said “yes,” then “no” — conflict noted.
  - Legs: Walking normal; no reported weakness in legs.
- Past medical history: Generally healthy. Had a “bad cold/flu-like” illness ~1 month ago lasting ~2 weeks after a night of heavy drinking.
- Medications:
  - Ibuprofen (dose/route/frequency not documented) as needed for muscle soreness/right-hand knuckle pain.
  - Vitamin D (dose/route/frequency not documented).
  - Iron supplement (dose/route/frequency not documented); poor adherence due to pill size.
  - Melatonin (dose/route/frequency not documented) intermittently for sleep.
- Family history:
  - Father: Hypothyroidism; unspecified autoimmune condition.
  - Mother: Type 2 diabetes, hypertension, hyperlipidemia.
  - No known family history of neurological conditions (per consult).
- Social history:
  - Exercises regularly; recently started boxing classes.
  - Right-hand dominant.
  - Plays piano.
  - One episode of heavy alcohol use preceding illness.
- Allergies: Not discussed.

Objective:
- Telehealth visit; no vitals recorded.
- Physical exam: Not documented.
- Investigations: None performed during consult.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Left upper limb numbness/tingling and weakness:
   - Assessment: Unilateral sensory symptoms and perceived weakness of the left arm with palmar digit 2–4 involvement; progressive over ~2 weeks.
   - Differential diagnosis: Boxing-related peripheral nerve/musculoskeletal injury; possible demyelinating disease (e.g., multiple sclerosis) — as discussed.
   - Investigations planned: Urgent neurology referral; brain imaging per neurology (clinician mentioned this may include a brain scan).
   - Treatment planned: No new medications initiated; steroids discussed as possible treatment only if diagnosis confirmed.
   - Relevant referrals: Urgent neurology.

2. Transient left-eye visual disturbance (resolved):
   - Assessment: Single episode of transient visual field loss in the left eye (~20 minutes) a few weeks prior.
   - Differential diagnosis: Possible demyelinating process (as discussed).
   - Investigations planned: To be evaluated under urgent neurology referral; may include brain imaging.
   - Treatment planned: None initiated pending specialist evaluation.
   - Safety-net: ED if visual symptoms recur or worsen.

Quality checks:
- Missing expected elements: Allergies not recorded; no vitals; no focused neurological exam documented (strength, reflexes, sensation, coordination); medication doses/routes/frequencies not documented; smoking status and routine alcohol intake not discussed.
- Internal conflicts: Neck pain reported as both “yes” and “no” — conflict noted.
- Transcript quality: Generally clear; minor conversational overlaps; no major inaudible sections.
